text:
Marathon Petroleum stock has fallen 0.95% today and 9% over the past week, driven by a confluence of negative signals for refining profitability. The core issue is that the refining industry's profit engine—the "crack spread," the gap between crude oil prices and refined product prices—has compressed sharply. While U.S. crude sits at $89.53 per barrel, gasoline and diesel inventories remain elevated (216 million and 105 million barrels respectively), and refineries are running near full capacity at 95.7%, limiting the ability to push refined product prices higher. This squeezes the margin that refiners pocket on each barrel processed.

The broader headwind is a shift in market positioning: a November 23 report noted that the "epic boom in refinery-related stocks is unwinding," suggesting investors are rotating away from the trade that powered energy stocks higher earlier this year. Geopolitical risks to Middle Eastern oil supply—Iran-backed attacks on Saudi refineries and U.S. tanker escorts in the Strait of Hormuz—have failed to push crude high enough to restore refining spreads, leaving Marathon's stock to absorb the unwinding without offsetting support.
